title: apache/commons-codec 43a9aa66: Hex decoding restricted to ASCII, after modelling the JDK
summary: A maintainer's commit that makes `Hex.toDigit` accept only ASCII hexadecimal digits, so that Unicode digits cannot bypass textual blocklists. Two false violations were traced to JDK classes JBMC has no model of and fixed with a forked charset models library and cache models; the new `toDigit` then proved in full, while the old one needs a model of `Character.digit`.
verdictLabel: ✓ new version proved; ⚠ old version needs a model of Character.digit
notes: The run recorded here needed the charset models (then a fork of the CProver models library) and the cache models on `--classpath` by hand; both now ship with jvmcontract (`lib/models`, `jvmcontract models`) and go on JBMC's class path by themselves, with a `Character.digit` model generated from the JDK's table that the old version's regression proof lacked. Before concluding anything from a violation in a class that reads a JDK class JBMC has no model of, check the trace for the stub and add a model.
A commit rather than a pull request: the commit and its parent were checked out into two worktrees and the skill's proofs run by hand.
Next in Commons Codec: `MurmurHash3` and `PureJavaCrc32`, whose classes read no charsets.

`toDigit` throws `DecoderException`, a checked exception, on a char that is no hex digit, and the equivalence harness catches only unchecked exceptions and `Error` (`harness::EXCEPTIONS`). So `equivalence` on `Hex#toDigit` ends in "an unexpected property failed: `EquivalenceHarness.check:(CI)V.1`" (JBMC's "no uncaught exception") until the harness tells declared exceptions apart, and a step that expects exit 1 for "the change, found" passes on that too: check for the found change instead. The old version's regression proof under `--assume 'ch == 1632'` holds under `--gaps strict` since the gap preflight asks JBMC's solver whether `String.format`'s stub is reached (VF-015, job `20261108-011411-vf-015-example-109-revisited-hex-todigit`).
provenance: A real change to a published library, verified with the /verify-bytecode skill; the report is this folder's README.md.
